title: Direct object pronouns: le, la, les
goal: By the end of this lesson you can replace a direct object with le, la, l' or les, put the pronoun in the right place in the present, the futur proche, the negative and the passé composé.

body: A direct object receives the action directly, with no preposition: *Je vois* **Marie**. *Je mange* **la pomme**. *J'aime* **les chiens**.
To avoid repeating it, French replaces it with a short pronoun: *le* (him, it, masculine), *la* (her, it, feminine), *les* (them). Before a vowel or silent h, *le* and *la* become *l'*.

learn.h: The pronoun goes before the verb
body: Unlike English (I see *him*), French puts the pronoun in front of the conjugated verb: *Je* **le** *vois*. *Tu* **la** *connais?* *Nous* **les** *invitons*.
In the negative, *ne* goes before the pronoun and *pas* after the verb: *Je* **ne le** *vois* **pas**. *Elle* **ne les** *aime* **pas**.
learn.tip: Pronoun and verb are glued together: ne + pronoun + verb + pas.

learn.h: With an infinitive: futur proche, vouloir, pouvoir
body: When there are two verbs, the pronoun goes in front of the verb it belongs to, which is the infinitive: *Je vais* **le** *faire*. *Tu peux* **la** *prendre*. *On veut* **les** *voir*.
Negative: *Je ne vais pas le faire.* The *ne…pas* wraps the first verb; the pronoun stays with the infinitive.
In the passé composé, the pronoun goes before the auxiliary *avoir*: *Je* **l'***ai vu*. *Tu* **les** *as achetés?* Negative: *Je ne l'ai pas vu.*

Notice the agreement: when the direct object comes before *avoir*, the past participle agrees with it in writing: *La lettre? Je l'ai écrit***e**. *Les clés? Je les ai trouvé***es**. We will practise this rule in detail in lesson 46.

learn.h: Me, te, nous, vous, and the imperative
body: The other direct object pronouns are the same as the reflexive ones: *me* (me), *te* (you), *nous* (us), *vous* (you): *Il* **me** *regarde*. *Je* **t'***aime*. *Elle* **nous** *invite*.
In a positive command, the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen: *Regarde-***le**! *Prends-***la**! *Achetez-***les**! In a negative command it goes back in front: *Ne* **le** *regarde pas!*

examples.fr: Tu connais Julie? Oui, je la connais bien.
examples.en: Do you know Julie? Yes, I know her well.

examples.fr: Le film? Je le regarde ce soir.
examples.en: The movie? I'm watching it tonight.

examples.fr: Mes clés? Je les cherche depuis une heure.
examples.en: My keys? I've been looking for them for an hour.

examples.fr: L'autobus? Je le prends tous les matins.
examples.en: The bus? I take it every morning.

examples.note: la becomes l' before a vowel

examples.en: We're going to invite them on Saturday.
examples.note: futur proche: the pronoun goes before the infinitive

examples.fr: Je peux la porter pour toi.
examples.en: I can carry it for you.
examples.note: la refers to a feminine noun, like la boîte

examples.fr: Ton courriel? Je l'ai lu hier.
examples.en: Your email? I read it yesterday.

examples.fr: Je ne l'ai pas vu de la journée.
examples.en: I haven't seen him all day.

examples.fr: Les photos? Je les ai envoyées ce matin.
examples.en: The photos? I sent them this morning.
examples.note: envoyées agrees with les photos (f pl)

examples.fr: Ma mère m'appelle tous les dimanches.
examples.en: My mother calls me every Sunday.
examples.note: me becomes m' before a vowel

examples.en: I'll wait for you in front of the corner store.
examples.note: attendre takes a direct object: no 'for' in French
positive command: pronoun after the verb

examples.fr: Ne la touche pas, elle est chaude.
examples.note: negative command: pronoun before the verb
écouter takes a direct object in French

quebec.intro: In everyday Quebec speech the e of je and le often disappears, so the pronoun gets squeezed against the verb: 'j'l'ai vu', 'j'les ai', 'j'la connais'. Write the full forms, but train your ear for the short ones.

items.note: ne dropped and je shortened; informal
j'vas = je vais in Quebec speech
t' for tu, plus the -tu question particle; informal

drills.q: Replace the object: 'Je regarde la télé.'
drills.why: Télé is feminine singular: la, placed before the verb.

drills.q: Where does the pronoun go? 'Je vais acheter les billets.'
drills.why: With two verbs, the pronoun goes before the infinitive.
Le becomes l' before the vowel of ai.

drills.q: Les enfants? Je ___ vois au parc. (them)
drills.en: The children? I see them at the park.
Your sister? I know her well.

drills.q: Ton livre? Je ___ ai oublié chez moi. (it)
drills.en: Your book? I forgot it at home.

drills.why: Me becomes m' before a vowel.

drills.en: I'm going to call her tonight.

drills.why: The pronoun goes before avoir; vue if 'it' is feminine.
Attendre takes a direct object: no word for 'for'.

vocab.ex: Je le vois. Je la vois.

pron.fr: je le vois / je les vois
pron.tip: le [luh] vs les [lé]: the vowel tells you singular or plural.
t' links to the verb: juh ta-TAHN.

dialogue.fr: As-tu vu mes clés? Je les cherche partout.
dialogue.en: Have you seen my keys? I'm looking everywhere for them.

dialogue.fr: Non, j'les ai pas vues. Tu les avais à matin?
dialogue.en: No, I haven't seen them. Did you have them this morning?

dialogue.fr: Oui, je les ai prises pour aller au dépanneur.
dialogue.en: Yes, I took them to go to the corner store.

dialogue.fr: Pis ton manteau? Tu l'as regardé?
dialogue.en: And your coat? Did you check it?

dialogue.fr: Oui, je l'ai regardé deux fois.
Attends… ton sac d'épicerie, il est où?
dialogue.en: Wait… your grocery bag, where is it?

dialogue.fr: Je l'ai laissé dans la cuisine. Ah! Les voilà! Elles sont dans le sac!
dialogue.en: I left it in the kitchen. Ah! There they are! They're in the bag!

questions.q: Where did A go with the keys this morning?

speak.prompt: Answer with a pronoun: 'Tu regardes la télé le soir? Tu connais tes voisins? Tu aimes le hockey?'
speak.model: Oui, je la regarde le soir. Non, je ne les connais pas bien. Oui, je l'aime beaucoup!

speak.prompt: Say three things you are going to do this weekend with a pronoun: 'Le ménage? Je vais le faire samedi.'
speak.model: Le ménage? Je vais le faire samedi. Mes amis? Je vais les voir dimanche. Ma mère? Je vais l'appeler.

speak.prompt: Say 'I saw him yesterday' in standard French, then the casual Quebec way.
speak.model: Je l'ai vu hier. / J'l'ai vu hier.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about objects you use every day (phone, car, keys, coffee…). Mention each object once, then refer to it with le, la or les.
write.model: Mon téléphone, je le regarde trop souvent. Je l'utilise même au lit! Mon café, je le bois sans sucre. Mes clés, je les perds tout le temps. Hier, je les ai cherchées pendant vingt minutes. Ma voiture, je la lave une fois par mois.

quiz.why: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb.
Robe is feminine; the pronoun sits before the infinitive acheter.

quiz.q: Which is correct in the passé composé?
quiz.why: Pronoun before avoir: je l'ai vu.
Positive command: verb + hyphen + pronoun. (La ferme! is a rude 'shut up'.)
Attendre = to wait for; t' = you.

quiz.q: Which sentence is negative and correct?
options: Je ne vais pas le faire.
Je ne le vais pas faire.
Je vais ne le pas faire.
Je ne vais le pas faire.
quiz.why: Ne…pas wraps vais; le stays before faire.

quiz.q: Why is it 'je les ai trouvées' (with -es)?
options: Because les (feminine plural) comes before avoir
quiz.why: A direct object placed before avoir makes the participle agree.
